content:
If You Cannot Stand Out, You May Be Left Behind

  • From an economic perspective, only 5% of people successfully create a life of freedom, while the remaining 95% continue struggling in the mire. What should we do now to avoid joining the 95% who struggle throughout their lives, rise above a world of mediocrity, and become part of the successful 5%?
  • Ninety-five percent of people reluctantly live lives they do not want. Although they hope to have more, they live with regret every day. They never discover that they could have become better people, done more, and had everything they wanted.
  • The four major areas of life are physical health, mental well-being, family, and finances.

Do Not Underestimate Yourself

  • “Rearview Mirror Syndrome”—constantly recalling past experiences: What you have done up to this point determines your current circumstances, but your future depends on the choices you make from now on.
  • Having no higher purpose than “staying alive”: Set a purpose for your life.
  • The “isolated incident” fallacy: Self-discipline determines the state of your life. Who you become is far more important than what you do right now, but who you become still depends on your current actions.
  • Lack of accountability: Accountability brings order to our lives, enables improvement and progress, and helps us achieve more.
  • A social circle that is too small: Our character tends to approach the average of the five people closest to us. Your life increasingly resembles the lives of those nearest to you. If you surround yourself with lazy people, weak people, and excuse-makers, you will inevitably become like them. Spend more time with positive, successful people. Their attitudes toward success and their habits will gradually influence you, and you will become increasingly successful.
  • Being half-hearted about personal development: Instead of spending time complaining about life, focus on personal development.
  • The “tomorrow after tomorrow” habit of procrastination: One of life’s saddest experiences is living with regret—regretting that you did not work harder or become the person you wanted to be. Remember this truth: “Now” matters more than any other time. Your actions today determine the direction and quality of your life tomorrow.
  • Do “miraculous” things and become exceptional: “One of life’s greatest tragedies is looking back as you approach death and realizing that you could have become a better person, done more, and had more.”

The Life S.A.V.E.R.S.

  • Purposeful Silence: With a strong desire, calm your mind. Release stress, anxiety, confusion, and agitation.
  • Genuine Affirmations: Repeat affirmations until they become faith. When faith becomes a profound conviction, everything begins to change.
  • Mental rehearsal through Visualization: Imagine what you will look and feel like after obtaining everything you want…
  • Exercise
  • Reading
  • Scribing
    • Clarify your thinking: Writing forces us to think more deeply. It can make your thoughts clearer, stimulate brainstorming, and help you solve difficult problems.
    • Capture inspiration: Journaling not only helps broaden your thinking but also prevents you from forgetting important ideas.
    • Review lessons learned: Journaling helps you revisit what you have learned.
    • Examine your progress.

Only Six Minutes Separate You from Your Ideal Self

  • Minute one: Silence, meditation, or gratitude.
  • Minute two: Read your affirmations aloud.
  • Minute three: Vividly imagine the future.
  • Minute four: Write down what you are grateful for.
  • Minute five: Quietly read one page of a book.
  • Minute six: Get moving.

“Your greatest adventure is living the life of your dreams.”

  • Increased income, a better quality of life, greater self-discipline, reduced mental stress, successful weight loss… all of these can happen to you.
  • First, you must spend time each day becoming the person you want to be: someone qualified and capable of continually creating and sustaining the success you desire.
  • “Your level of success will seldom exceed your level of personal development, because the level you reach as a person determines the level of success you create.”

中文版

你如果不能出众，就可能出局

  • 从经济学的视角来看，只有 5% 的人能够成功地创造自由的人生，而剩下 95% 的人将继续在泥沼中挣扎。那么，我们现在应该怎么做，才能避免沦为终身为生活挣扎的 95%，从平庸的世界脱颖而出，成为 5% 的人生赢家？
  • 世界上 95% 的人都无奈地过着自己并不想要的生活。虽然他们希望自己能够拥有更多，但每天都生活在悔恨之中。他们永远也不知道自己原本可以成为更好的人、做更多的事，并拥有自己想要的一切。
  • 人生四大命题：生理、心理、家庭和财务。

不要低估自己

  • “后视镜综合征”——不断地回忆过去的经历：你在现阶段的所作所为决定了自己的处境，但未来则取决于你从今开始所做的选择。
  • 没有比“活着”更高的目标：设立人生目标。
  • “孤立事件”谬误：自律决定生活状态。你将成为什么样的人远比现在要做的事情更重要，但你将成为什么样的人依然取决于目前的行动。
  • 缺乏责任感：责任感能够让我们的生活变得秩序井然，实现提升和进步，取得更高的成就。
  • 朋友圈太小：我们的人格倾向于接近生活中 5 个最亲密之人的平均水平。你跟谁最亲近，你的生活就越像谁。如果你的身边都是懒鬼、弱者、爱找借口的人，你也不可避免地沦为那种人。所以，多花时间与积极、成功的人相处。他们对待成功的态度和习惯会慢慢地影响你，你也会变得越来越成功。
  • 对个人发展“三心二意”：与其花时间抱怨生活，不如专注于个人发展。
  • 明日复明日的“拖延症”：人生最可悲的一件事就是活在悔恨当中，后悔自己当初没有更努力，没有成为自己想要成为的人。记住这个真理：“现在”比任何时刻都更重要。你今天的行动决定了明天的人生方向和生活品质。
  • 做“神奇”的事，成为出众的人：“人生最大的悲剧之一，就是当你临终回首往事时，发现自己其实可以成为更好的人，做得更多，并拥有更多。”

人生拯救计划

  • 保持目的性的心静（Silence）：带着强烈的愿望，让内心平静下来，去掉压力、焦虑、迷茫和心烦意乱。
  • 真正的自我肯定（Affirmations）：不断地肯定，直到变成信仰。当信仰变成深刻信念，一切就会发生变化。
  • 内心演练（Visualization）：想象自己已经得到想要的一切后的样子……
  • 锻炼（Exercise）
  • 阅读（Reading）
  • 书写（Scribing）
    • 思维更加清晰：写作会迫使我们更深入地思考，可以让你的思维变得更清晰，激起头脑风暴，帮你解决难题。
    • 捕获灵感：写日记不仅能帮你拓展思维，还可以防止你遗忘重要的灵感。
    • 回顾经验教训：写日记可以帮你回顾自己所学的知识。
    • 检阅自己的进步。

你和理想的自己只差 6 分钟

  • 第一分钟：心静、冥想或感恩。
  • 第二分钟：大声朗诵自我肯定宣言。
  • 第三分钟：尽情地想象未来。
  • 第四分钟：写下让自己感激的事情。
  • 第五分钟：静静地读一页书。
  • 第六分钟：动起来。

“你最大的冒险，就是过梦想中的生活。”

  • 收入增加、生活质量提高、更加自律、心理减压、减肥成功……这一切都可能发生在你身上。
  • 首先，你必须每天花时间成为自己想要成为的人：有资格和能力不断创造、维持自己想要的成功。
  • “你的成功水平很少能超过自己的个人发展水平，因为你是什么水平，就会创造什么水平的成功。”

title: Rich Dad Poor Dad: Reading Notes
content:
Lesson One: The Rich Do Not Work for Money

  • Find ways to make money generate more money instead of working for a fixed salary and paying taxes. Financial freedom is reached when passive income covers your needs.
  • An asset puts money into your pocket. A liability takes money out of your pocket.

Lesson Two: Learn Financial Literacy

  • Real assets:
    1. Businesses that can operate normally without my presence. I own them, but other people operate and manage them. If I have to work there, it is not my business; it is my profession.
    2. Stocks.
    3. Bonds.
    4. Mutual funds.
    5. Income-generating real estate.
    6. Notes (IOUs).
    7. Royalties, such as those from music, manuscripts, and patents.
    8. Anything else that has value, generates income or has the potential to appreciate, and has a ready market.

Lesson Three: Mind Your Own Business

Lesson Four: The History of Taxes and the Power of Corporations

  • Use corporations to reduce taxes:
    1. Tax advantages. A corporation can do many things an individual cannot, such as paying expenses with pre-tax income, including car insurance, repairs, membership fees, meals, and more.
    2. Employees earn money, pay taxes, and live on what remains; corporations earn money, spend it, and pay taxes only on what remains.
  • Financial literacy helps you read financial statements and identify a business’s strengths and weaknesses.
  • Investing is what I call the science of making money generate more money.
  • Understand markets, the science of supply and demand. Whether an investment ultimately makes sense depends on current market conditions.

Lesson Five: The Rich Invent Money

  • Laws and regulations: Become familiar with laws concerning accounting and corporations, as well as state and national regulations. We must play the “game” by the rules.

Lesson Six: Work to Learn—Do Not Work for Money

  • When looking for a job, young people should consider what they can learn from it, not just how much they can earn.
  • The management skills needed for success include:
    1. Managing cash flow.
    2. Managing systems, including yourself, your time, and your family.
    3. Managing people.

Seek new ideas. To find inspiration for investments, start taking action.

中文版

第一课：富人不为钱工作

  • 想办法让钱生钱，而不是为了固定工资工作和交税。直到被动收入能够覆盖自己的需求，就实现财富自由了。
  • 资产是能把钱放进你口袋里的东西。负债是把钱从你口袋里取走的东西。

第二课：学习财务知识

  • 真正的资产：
    1. 不需我到场就可以正常运作的业务。我拥有它们，但由别人经营和管理。如果我必须在那里工作，那它就不是我的事业，而是我的职业。
    2. 股票。
    3. 债券。
    4. 共同基金。
    5. 能够产生收入的房地产。
    6. 票据（借据）。
    7. 版税，如音乐、手稿、专利的版税。
    8. 其他任何有价值、可产生收入或有增值潜力，并且有很好销路的东西。

第三课：关注自己的事业

第四课：税收的历史和公司的力量

  • 通过公司来避税：
    1. 减税优惠。公司可以做许多个人无法做的事，例如用税前收入支付开支，包括车险、修理费、会员费、餐饮费等等。
    2. 雇员挣钱、纳税，并靠剩下的钱为生；企业挣钱、花钱，并只为剩下来的钱缴税。
  • 财务知识能帮助你读懂财务报表，还能让你辨别一项生意的优势和劣势。
  • 投资，我把它称为钱生钱的科学。
  • 了解市场，它是供给与需求的科学。一项投资究竟有无意义，最终取决于当前的市场状况。

第五课：富人的投资

  • 法律规章：要熟悉有关会计、公司方面的法律，以及各州和国家的法规。我们必须按规则来进行“游戏”。

第六课：学会不为钱工作

  • 年轻人在找工作时要看能从中学到什么，而不是只看能挣多少钱。
  • 成功所必需的管理技能包括：
    1. 对现金流的管理。
    2. 对系统的管理，包括你本人、时间及家庭。
    3. 对人员的管理。

寻找新的思想。为了寻找投资的灵感，开始行动。

title: Advice from The Barefoot Investor
content:
Some tips I should remember from the book The Barefoot Investor.

  1. Banks: Choose one with no monthly fee that offers a higher interest rate.
  2. Superannuation: Check the annual fee and choose a fund that invests in an ETF index.
  3. Private insurance: Pay a higher excess ($500 or $750) to lower your monthly premium.
    • Do not automatically renew insurance. Compare providers and switch if necessary.
  4. Property: Buy with a 20% deposit so that you do not need to pay LMI, which uses your money to protect the lender.
  5. Stocks: Become a business owner and reinvest dividends where possible.

中文版

我应该记住的《赤脚投资者》一书中的一些建议。

  1. 银行：选择不收月费且利率较高的银行。
  2. 养老金：检查年费，并选择投资 ETF 指数的基金。
  3. 私人保险：支付较高的免赔额（$500 或 $750），以降低每月保费。
    • 不要自动续保。比较不同保险机构，并在必要时更换。
  4. 房产：支付 20% 的首付购房，这样就不必支付 LMI；LMI 是用你的钱来保护贷款机构的保险。
  5. 股票：成为企业的所有者，并尽可能将股息再投资。

title: Deep Work Rules: Reading Notes
content:
1. Deep Work: Deep Work Rules

The Ideas

  1. Deep work is valuable.
  2. Deep work is rare.
  3. Deep work is meaningful.

The Rules

  1. Work deeply.

    In a prolonged, distraction-free state, tackle batches of difficult but important intellectual work.

  2. Embrace boredom.
  3. Quit social media.
  4. Drain the shallows.

    During your leisure time, do not let random matters capture your attention. Instead, actively think about how you should spend your day.

2. The Science of the Lazy Brain

Ego depletion: When our self-control is depleted, we are more likely to give in to everyday temptations. Scientists call this self-control fatigue “ego depletion.” If you want to change your behavior, make sure the goals you set are within a reasonable range.

Overcompensation: When we are tense, stressed, or in a bad mood, the brain seeks compensation, such as overeating or revenge shopping.

Duration rather than intensity: Our bodies do not need brief, high-intensity exercise; they need moderate-intensity training of sufficient duration.

Deep Work

  • Shallow work includes doing work you already know, frequently attending meetings and events, replying to emails, and so on. This kind of work only makes a person look busy; it creates no new value and is easy to replicate or replace.
    • Reasons:
      1. The principle of least resistance: everyone wants to avoid difficulty and choose simple tasks.
      2. Busyness is treated as a proxy for productivity.
      3. Internet-centrism: being consumed by online entertainment.
  1. Choose a mode:
    • Monastic mode: isolate yourself for deep work and cut off channels of contact with the outside world.
    • Rhythmic mode: do the same thing at a fixed time each day to establish a rhythm.
    • Bimodal mode: divide your time into two parts, reserving one explicitly for deep work and the other for shallow work. During deep-work periods, bimodal workers pursue intense, distraction-free concentration.
    • Journalistic mode: enter a state of deep work anytime and anywhere, shifting into it whenever free time appears.
  2. Internalize the habit and practice deliberately.
  3. Use quantitative metrics.
  4. Appropriately reduce working hours and meditate.

中文版

1.《深度工作》：深度工作准则

核心观点

  1. 深度工作是有价值的。
  2. 深度工作是少见的。
  3. 深度工作是有意义的。

准则

  1. 工作要深入。

    在长时间无干扰的状态下，批量解决困难却重要的智力工作。

  2. 拥抱无聊。
  3. 远离社交媒体。
  4. 摒弃浮浅。

    在个人娱乐的时候，不要被随意的事务吸引，而是主动思考我该如何度过一天。

2.《懒惰脑科学》

自我损耗：当我们的自控力缺失时，更容易经不住日常诱惑。科学家把这种自控力疲劳命名为“自我损耗”。如果你希望改变自己的行为，就要确保自己制定的目标在合理范围内。

过度补偿：当我们精神紧张、压力大或心情不好时，大脑会寻找补偿，比如大吃大喝或者报复性购物。

时长而非强度：我们的身体并不需要短时间、高强度的体育锻炼，而是需要达到一定时长的中等强度训练。

深度工作

  • 浮浅工作包括做自己已经熟悉的工作、频繁参加各类会议活动、回复邮件等等。这类工作只会让一个人看起来很忙，并不会创造新价值，且容易被复制和替换。
    • 原因：
      1. 最小阻力原则：人人都想避免困难，选择简单的任务。
      2. 忙碌代表生产力。
      3. 网络中心主义：被网络娱乐吞噬。
  1. 选择模式：
    • 禁欲模式：与外界隔绝，进行深度工作，切断与外界联系的媒介。
    • 节奏模式：每天在某个固定时间做同一件事，形成节奏。
    • 双峰模式：将时间分成两块，一块明确用于深度工作，另一块用于浮浅工作。在深度工作的时间里，双峰工作者会追求高强度、无干扰的专注。
    • 记者模式：随时随地进入深度工作状态，一有空闲时间就进入深度工作状态。
  2. 内化习惯，刻意练习。
  3. 使用量化指标。
  4. 适当减少工作时间并进行冥想。

title: Living Without Fatigue
content:
Excerpts from Living Without Fatigue by Takafumi Kudo (Japan).

  • Drink a glass of milk in the morning to improve sleep quality.
  • Eat protein-rich foods in the morning, such as milk, fish, soy products, and nuts.
  • If you sleep well but still feel tired upon waking, take a 20-minute nap during the day so that the day’s fatigue is relieved that same day.
  • When you feel upset or restless, have a kimchi hot pot.
  • Do not snack after 10 p.m. Eating between 10 p.m. and 2 a.m. not only prolongs gastrointestinal activity but also reduces sleep quality, increases the metabolic burden, and makes weight gain more likely.
  • To avoid the temptation of late-night food, it is best not to stay up late and to go to bed early.
  • Around 2 p.m., when you are less likely to gain weight, you may have a snack.
  • After 3 p.m., replace plain water with lemon water or other tart fruits.
  • Do not snack between meals. Feeling hungry causes the stomach to secrete ghrelin, which activates mitochondria and rejuvenates cells.
  • High-GI (glycemic index) foods, such as toast, rice, and potatoes, can increase fatigue. Eat more brown staple foods such as brown rice and whole-wheat bread.
  • Beer can relieve premenstrual syndrome and help prevent hair loss and graying. Drink no more than 350 mL per day.
  • Finish dinner before 9 p.m. and choose low-fat foods.

中文版

摘抄自《不疲劳的生活》，作者：[日]工藤孝文。

  • 早上喝一杯牛奶，提高睡眠质量。
  • 早上吃富含蛋白质的食物，如牛奶、鱼类、豆制品和坚果等。
  • 建议睡得很好但醒来依然觉得累的人，白天小憩 20 分钟，当天的疲劳当天消除。
  • 心烦意乱的时候吃个泡菜锅吧。
  • 晚上 10 点后不要加餐。晚 10 点至凌晨 2 点吃东西，不仅会延长肠胃蠕动时间，还会导致睡眠质量下降、增加代谢负担，并且更容易发胖。
  • 为了避开深夜的美食诱惑，最好不要熬夜，早点睡觉。
  • 下午 2 点前后不易发胖，可以加餐。
  • 下午 3 点后，用柠檬水或其他酸味水果代替凉白开。
  • 三餐之间不要加餐。空腹感会使胃分泌胃饥饿素，激活线粒体，使细胞重返年轻。
  • 高 GI（升糖指数）食品会增加疲惫感，例如吐司面包、大米和土豆。多吃糙米、全麦面包等茶色主食。
  • 啤酒能缓解经前综合征，预防脱发、白发等，一天最多 350 mL。
  • 晚餐在晚上 9 点前吃完，选择脂肪少的食物。

title: 2026: After Leaving My Comfort Zone, the World Suddenly Grew Bigger
content:
2026: The Year I Left My Comfort Zone and the World Became Bigger

During my first seven years in Australia, I hardly travelled at all.

My life gradually became smaller, and I spent a long time being drained by an unhealthy relationship. The days continued to pass, but when I looked back, very few memories felt truly mine.

In 2026, I finally began stepping outside my comfort zone.

The year is not over yet, but it already feels richer than the previous seven or eight years combined.

Why Time Feels Faster as We Grow Older

As a child, a single day felt long, and a year seemed almost endless.

As an adult, life appears to move in fast-forward. One week follows another, and an entire year can end before it feels as though anything happened.

One explanation stayed with me: time does not simply speed up. Adults often repeat the same routines—travelling to the same workplace, doing familiar tasks, and returning home to similar evenings. When the brain records fewer distinctive memories, that period becomes compressed when we look back on it.

Childhood is full of firsts: a first day at school, a first friendship, a first visit to an unfamiliar place. Each new experience creates a marker in memory, which may be why those years feel so long.

Perhaps 2026 has felt so rich because it has contained so many firsts.

I cannot stop time from moving, but I can give it more memories to leave behind.

I Started by Moving My Body

I began going to the gym consistently. I also tried Pilates and running in the park.

In the past, being unfamiliar with something—or being afraid of doing it badly—was enough to stop me from beginning. Now I am learning that I do not need to feel ready first. I can simply show up and try, and allow my strength and confidence to follow.

Fitness has given me more than physical change. It has shown me that I can care for my body and gradually reshape my life.

I Moved Closer to People and the Stage

I attended television recordings as an audience member and even tried being a contestant. I took painting lessons, completed a two-month improvisation course, and practised starting conversations with strangers.

I also began going alone to different comedy clubs to watch people tell their stories onstage. Eventually, I enrolled in a two-month stand-up comedy course of my own.

I met new people, and my social circle slowly grew.

I used to think the stage belonged only to people who were naturally outgoing and funny. Now I understand that courage does not mean feeling no fear. It means taking one more step while still feeling nervous.

I Still Don’t Have the Answer to Dating

This year, I tried speed dating, slow dating, and online dating.

I genuinely hoped to find a long-term relationship and ended up disappointed. Even now, I am not completely certain what kind of relationship I want.

The experience did teach me something about myself: I can admire another person’s freedom, independence, or ability to enjoy his own company, then build a filter around him because I like what those qualities represent.

Instead of worshipping the life someone else appears to have, I can build those qualities into my own life.

I Can Become Someone I Think Is Cool

I thought people who rode motorcycles looked cool, so I signed up for motorcycle lessons.

Once I began learning, that distant sense of admiration became smaller. Many things that look impressive are not reserved for a special kind of person.

I can learn them too.

I can become someone I think is cool.

My First Solo Trip to Bali

This year, I finally travelled to Bali by myself.

Before leaving, I imagined dating and meeting handsome men. Once I arrived, I tried many completely different things instead: paragliding with strangers, going to a bar alone, working out, riding motorcycles, sitting beside the ocean, and trying to make new friends.

In the end, I did not make many lasting friendships.

But I discovered that a journey does not need to produce a crowd of new friends to be successful. Returning to my room alone, eating alone, and choosing my next destination alone could also feel peaceful.

I did not find a relationship in Bali. Instead, I returned loving my own life more and appreciating everything I already had.

The World Suddenly Became Bigger

After I returned from Bali, my company offered me an opportunity to study in the United States.

Suddenly, the world felt enormous and exciting.

For years, I seemed to stand in the same place, believing life consisted only of work, relationships, and the worries directly in front of me. Once I stepped outside, I found gyms, stages, painting, motorcycles, travel, strangers, and so many places I had not yet reached.

Staying Soft After Seeing the World

While travelling, I met people who had already visited many places and experienced many extraordinary things.

After seeing so much of the world, some of them no longer seemed to admire romantic love, and very little could genuinely excite them. Perhaps when novelty and stimulation become ordinary, it becomes harder to feel moved.

I do not want that to happen to me.

No matter how many countries I visit or how much of the world I eventually see, I hope I keep a soft heart. I want to remain capable of love and kindness—and still feel happy because of a sunset, an ocean breeze, a delicious meal, or a small act of generosity from a stranger.

Being worldly should not mean becoming indifferent. Perhaps rich experiences should not teach us to say, “Is that all?” They should help us understand different lives and appreciate our own more deeply.

I want to keep exploring outward without losing my ability to feel joy within.

After seeing the world, I still want to be grateful for it.

Leaving my comfort zone did not magically make my life perfect.

I still feel lonely. Relationships still hurt me. I still become afraid and uncertain about where to go next.

But now I know that even when nobody comes with me, I can still leave.

A life cannot be measured only in years. Sometimes one year lived deliberately can leave more memories than seven years spent repeating the same routine.

In 2026, I did not find every answer.

But I finally began living again.

中文版

在澳大利亚生活的前七年，我几乎没有出去旅行过。

我的生活慢慢变得封闭，也在一段很糟糕的关系里消耗了很长时间。日子一直在过，但回头看时，好像没有留下多少真正属于自己的记忆。

到了 2026 年，我终于开始走出舒适圈。

这一年还没有结束，但它好像已经比过去七八年加起来都更精彩。

为什么长大以后，时间过得越来越快

小时候，总觉得一天很长，一年更是遥远得看不到尽头。

长大以后，时间却像突然按下了快进键。一周接着一周，一年好像什么都没有发生就结束了。

后来我看到一种解释：并不只是时间变快了，而是成年后的我们经常重复同样的生活。去同一个地方上班，做熟悉的事情，回家以后继续相似的夜晚。大脑没有留下足够多的新记忆，回头看时，那段时间就被压缩成了模糊的一小块。

小的时候，很多事情都是第一次。第一次上学，第一次交朋友，第一次去陌生的地方。每一个“第一次”都会留下清晰的记忆，所以童年显得格外漫长。

也许 2026 年让我感觉如此丰富，正是因为这一年里有太多第一次。

我不能让时间停下来，但我可以让走过的时间留下更多痕迹。

先让身体动起来

我开始规律地去健身房，也尝试了普拉提和公园跑步。

以前的我可能会因为不熟悉、怕做不好，干脆不开始。现在我慢慢发现，很多事情不需要等到准备好了才去做。先出现，先尝试，身体和信心都会慢慢跟上来。

健身带给我的不只是外形变化。它让我感觉自己有能力照顾好身体，也有能力一点点改变生活。

去靠近舞台和人群

我去电视节目录制现场当过观众，也尝试做过竞赛选手。我去学画画，上了两个月的即兴表演课程，还开始练习主动和陌生人说话。

我也开始一个人去不同的脱口秀俱乐部，看别人站在台上讲自己的故事。

后来，我给自己报名了一个两个月的脱口秀课程。

我认识了一些新朋友，社交圈也一点点扩大。以前觉得只有那些天生外向、特别有趣的人才适合站上舞台，现在才明白，勇气并不是不紧张，而是紧张的时候仍然愿意往前走一步。

关于约会，我仍然没有答案

今年我也体验了线下快速约会、慢速约会和线上约会。

我曾经认真期待一段长期关系，最后却很失望。到现在，我甚至还没有完全想明白，自己究竟想寻找怎样的关系。

但这个过程至少让我看见：我很容易羡慕一个人身上拥有的自由、独立和与自己相处的能力，然后在喜欢对方时，为他加上一层滤镜。

与其崇拜别人拥有的生活，我也可以慢慢建立自己的生活。

我也可以成为很酷的人

我觉得骑摩托车的人很酷，所以自己报名学习了摩托车。

当我真的开始学习以后，那种遥不可及的崇拜感反而减少了。原来很多看起来很厉害的事情，并不是某些人的专属。

我也可以学会。

我也可以成为自己觉得很酷的人。

第一次独自去巴厘岛

今年，我终于一个人去了巴厘岛。

出发前，我本来还想着约会、认识帅哥。真正到了以后，我却尝试了很多完全不同的东西：跟陌生人去玩滑翔伞，一个人去酒吧，去健身房，坐摩托车，在海边发呆，也试着认识新朋友。

最后，我并没有真正交到多少朋友。

但我发现，旅行不一定要靠认识很多人来证明它成功。一个人回到房间、一个人吃饭、一个人决定下一站去哪里，也可以很自在。

我没有在巴厘岛找到一段关系，却发现自己更爱原来的生活，也更珍惜自己已经拥有的一切。

世界突然变大了

从巴厘岛回来以后，公司又给了我一次去美国学习的机会。

我突然感觉，世界真的很大，也很精彩。

以前的我好像一直站在同一个地方，以为人生只有眼前的工作、关系和烦恼。真正走出去以后才发现，生活还有健身房、舞台、画画、摩托车、旅行、陌生人和很多尚未抵达的地方。

见过世界以后，仍然保持柔软

旅行中，我也遇见过一些已经看过很多地方、经历过很多事情的人。

他们见过更大的世界以后，好像不再羡慕浪漫的爱情，也很少有什么事情能够让他们真正兴奋。也许当新鲜和刺激变成日常，人会越来越难被打动。

但我不希望自己变成那样。

我希望无论以后去过多少国家、见过多大的世界，依然保留一颗柔软的心。依然愿意爱人，愿意善良，会因为一次日落、一阵海风、一顿好吃的饭，或者陌生人的一点善意而开心。

见多识广不应该意味着冷漠。真正丰富的经历，也许不是让人觉得“不过如此”，而是让人更理解不同的生活，也更懂得珍惜。

我希望自己不断向外探索，却不会失去内心感受幸福的能力。

看过世界以后，依然对世界心存感激。

走出舒适圈以后，我的生活并没有突然变得完美。

我仍然会孤独，会在关系里受伤，会害怕，也会不知道下一步应该去哪里。

但现在的我知道，即使没有人陪我，我也可以出发。

生命不一定要用年份来衡量。有时候，认真生活一年，真的可以比重复过去七年留下更多记忆。

2026 年，我没有找到所有答案。

但我终于重新开始生活了。

title: Atomic Habits: Taking Control of Your Habits
content:
• Habits are the compound interest of self-improvement. Over time, a tiny improvement can create an astonishing difference. If you improve by 1% every day for a year, you will be 37 times better by the end.
  • Even with genuine effort and occasional bursts of motivation, maintaining a good habit for several days in a row is often difficult. Habits such as exercising, meditating, journaling, and cooking may be manageable for a day or two, but soon become a nuisance.
  • Yet once habits form, they follow us everywhere and are hard to shake—especially bad ones. Despite our strong intentions, it is still difficult to quit habits such as eating junk food, watching too much television, procrastinating, and smoking.
  • Changing habits is challenging for two reasons: (1) we try to change the wrong thing, and (2) we try to change our habits in the wrong way.
  • True behavioural change is identity change. You may begin a habit because of some motivation, but the only reason you will maintain it over the long term is that it has become part of your identity.

中文版

  • 习惯是自我提高的复利。随着时间的推移，一点小小的改进就能带来惊人的不同。如果你一年内每天都能进步 1%，到结束时，你将会进步 37 倍。
  • 即使有真实的努力和偶尔爆发的十足冲劲，要连续几天保持好习惯往往很难做到。像健身、冥想、写日记和烹饪这样的习惯，保持一两天还行，接下来就成了烦心事。
  • 然而，一旦你养成了习惯，它们就会如影随形、挥之不去，尤其是那些不良嗜好。尽管我们有强烈的愿望，但还是很难戒掉一些不良习惯，如吃垃圾食品、沉溺于看电视、做事拖拉和吸烟。
  • 改变习惯之举颇具挑战性，原因有两个：（1）我们没有找对试图改变的东西；（2）我们试图以错误的方式改变我们的习惯。
  • 真正的行为改变是身份的改变。你可能会出于某种动机而培养一种习惯，但让你长期保持这种习惯的唯一原因，是它已经与你的身份融为一体。

title: Reflections on Life
content:
One

I started clearing out some old belongings and came across a diary I once kept. On October 9, 2012, I wrote that I wanted to study abroad but worried that I did not have enough money or good enough grades.

Looking back now, I used the savings from several years of work and the money I earned from part-time jobs abroad to complete my postgraduate degree. I then spent three years trying a job I loved, but the pay was so low that I eventually had to give it up and choose work related to my degree. I really wish I could tell my younger self: live in the present, keep your feet on the ground, and the things you want will slowly come true.

Two

Learn to embrace each present moment. In the end, we often discover that it is the accumulation of one moment after another that completes our past and creates our future.

中文版

一

开始清理以前的东西，翻到自己曾经的日记。2012 年 10 月 9 日这天，我写下了想去国外读书，但是没钱、没有好成绩的顾虑。

现在回头来看，靠着工作了几年的积蓄和在国外兼职，我已经读完研究生，并且尝试了三年自己喜欢的工作，最后因为薪水太低不得不放弃，而选择了专业对口的工作。真想对当时的自己说：过好当下，脚踏实地，你想要的都会慢慢实现的。

二

学会把握每个当下。到最后我们往往会发现，正是那一个又一个当下的累积，圆满了我们的过去，成就了我们的未来。

title: A Life Without Regrets
content:
Life — In Memory of My Beloved Uncle, 25/2/2023

  • In the first half of my life, I never thought about the meaning of life. I simply followed the expected path, waiting to grow up, go to school, work, get married, and have children, as if that were simply how life was meant to unfold.

  • When I was very young, I witnessed many deaths and attended many funerals, so I became especially afraid of dying. Even watching a little of a horror show would leave me too frightened to go outside or sleep at night.

  • As I grew into adulthood and began to understand the world, I felt deeply insecure because I was neither a top student nor a graduate of a prestigious university, and my job was only average. I desperately wanted to meet many people and understand more of the world.

  • It was only after going abroad that I discovered how rich and varied different lives could be. I learned that not every school requires ideological and political education, that even if you look ordinary, many people may still call you beautiful, and that you can be respected whatever work you do.

  • I began picking up my broken English and slowly integrating into society. Truly becoming part of a new environment taught me that I still had to keep working for whatever I wanted.

  • I also began loving myself. I started dating handsome men I had never imagined dating before and realised that making myself happy was what mattered most in life. I did not need to live through other people’s eyes, and I gradually lost the urge to keep trying to understand everyone else.

  • Although I still do not have much money, I am healthy and happy. I have also begun thinking about what I can do to help others and give back to society.

  • The older I get, the more I love myself. I have also suddenly realised that time is the cruelest thing of all: someone who was vivid and alive yesterday can be in another world today, as if they had never existed. When celebrities or political leaders die, at least many records of them remain. When ordinary people disappear, it is like a drop of water entering the ocean, never to be seen again.

  • In the long river of life, it turns out that death still cannot be escaped. It separates you from the people you love, making everything that happened between you feel like a dream.

  • Life is unpredictable. We cannot control life and death, illness, or wealth. Even after living for many years, I am still not very good at facing death.

  • Life is short, so enjoy it while you can.

I dedicate this piece to my departed loved ones. May we all have lived lives without regret.

中文版

人生——纪念我亲爱的叔叔，2023 年 2 月 25 日

  • 在人生的前半场，从没想过人生的意义，只是按部就班地生活着，等待着长大、上学、工作、结婚、生子，仿佛人生本就该如此。

  • 很小的时候，见过很多人的生死，参加过很多次葬礼，所以特别害怕自己死了。但凡看了一点恐怖的电视剧，晚上就吓得不敢出门、不敢睡觉。

  • 在我开始成人、认识世界的时候，因为不是学霸，也不是名校毕业，工作也一般般，整个人就特别自卑，特别想认识很多人，想更多地了解这个世界。

  • 去了国外，才发现不同人生的精彩。原来上学不是都必须学思想政治课的；原来你长相普通，很多人也会说你漂亮；无论你从事什么工作，都会受到尊重。

  • 开始捡起自己破烂的英语，开始慢慢地融入社会。真正融入新的环境，才明白原来想得到什么，还是需要靠自己不断努力。

  • 也开始自己爱自己，开始跟以前从未想过的帅哥们约会，开始发现人生让自己开心才最重要，没有必要活在他人的眼中，也就失去了想去了解他人的欲望。

  • 虽然现在还是没有钱，但是健康、快乐。也开始想着可以做些什么，来帮助他人、回馈社会。

  • 越长大，越爱自己，也突然意识到，时间是最残忍的。昨天还鲜活的人，今天就已经去了另一个世界，仿佛从来没有存在过。明星政要不在了，至少还有很多记录；而普通人消逝了，就像一滴水汇入了大海，再也不见踪影。

  • 原来人生的长河中，躲不掉的还是死亡。它把你爱的人和你隔开，仿佛你们之间发生的一切只是一场梦。

  • 人生无常，控制不了生死，控制不了疾病，控制不了财富。活了很多年，还是不太擅长应对死亡。

  • 人生苦短，及时行乐。

以此文纪念我逝去的亲人，愿我们都有过不悔的人生。

title: The Habits of the Wealthy
content:
The Habits of the Wealthy — Thomas C. Greey

  1. Read and learn every day instead of seeking entertainment. Teach yourself and improve through biographies of successful people and books about personal growth, self-cultivation, and history.
  2. Exercise consistently for more than 30 minutes every day.
  3. Enjoy meeting successful people who have clear goals, optimism, enthusiasm, and a positive mindset.
  4. Pursue your own dreams and goals.
  5. Keep getting up early, complete the three most important tasks, and take control of your life.
  6. Build multiple sources of income.
  7. Have a mentor in life.
  8. Maintain a positive attitude toward life.
  9. Do not follow the crowd. Stand out, create your own circle, and let others join it.
  10. Be polite in your conduct.
  11. Help other people succeed.
  12. Spend 15–30 minutes every day thinking, meditating, or jogging.
  13. Ask for feedback, and do not be afraid of criticism.

中文版

《富有的习惯》——Thomas C. Greey

  1. 每天阅读和学习，而不是娱乐。自学、提升，阅读成功人士自传以及个人修养、成长类和历史类的书。
  2. 坚持运动，每天大于 30 分钟。
  3. 乐于结识成功人士：目标明确、乐观热情、心态积极。
  4. 追求自己的梦想和目标。
  5. 坚持早起，完成最重要的 3 件事，掌控生活。
  6. 建立多重收入来源。
  7. 有自己的人生导师。
  8. 保持积极的人生态度。
  9. 不从众，让自己突出，创造你的圈子，让别人加入。
  10. 举止礼貌。
  11. 帮助他人成功。
  12. 每天花 15–30 分钟思考、冥想和慢跑。
  13. 寻求反馈，不害怕批评。

title: CKA Exam Notes and Experience — February 2023
content:
View resources

  • Use k api-resources to get the names of Kubernetes resources.

ETCD backup and restore

  • endpoint?
  • when restore, change etcd files location in hostPath
    vi /etc/kubernetes/etcd.yaml

Monitoring and logging

  • Metrics Server provides CPU and memory metrics: k top nodes, k top pods —containers=true.
  • Use crictl commands to inspect logs and containers.
  • To stream service logs, use journalctl -u kubelet -f.

DaemonSet vs deployment vs StatefulSet

  • A DaemonSet runs pods on all nodes, with at most one pod on each node. It is suitable for system-level applications such as log collection and resource monitoring; for example, Kube-proxy.
  • A StatefulSet is similar to a ReplicaSet, but it can manage pod startup order and assigns each pod a unique identity to preserve its state.

podAntiAffinity

  • Use topologySpreadConstraints to run workloads only on worker nodes.
  • With requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution, the scheduler can schedule a pod only when the rule is satisfied. This is similar to nodeSelector, but its syntax is more expressive.
  • Node Affinity.

Ephemeral volumes

  • emptyDir, which is erased when a pod is removed.

Service CIDR range—> static-pod, kube-apiserver.yaml

  • cat /etc/kubernetes/manifests/kube-apiserver.yaml | grep range
  • /etc/kubernetes/manifests/kube-apiserver.yaml : –service-cluster-ip-range
  • /etc/kubernetes/manifests/kube-controller-manager.yaml : –service-cluster-ip-range

Upgrade a cluster

kubeadm version
kubelet version
service kubelet status
systemctl daemon-reload && systemctl restart kubelet

Drain node01. A forceful drain of the node will delete any pod that is not part of a ReplicaSet.
Run kubectl cordon node01. This ensures that no new pods are scheduled on this node, while existing pods are not affected.

Add a node to the cluster

Use kubeadm token create to generate the node join command.

  1. On the control-plane node, run kubeadm token create --print-join-command.
  2. On the worker node, execute the output from the command above.

Certificate

  • View certificate details: openssl x509 -noout -text -in ./server.crt.
  • Check certificate expiration with the kubeadm command: kubeadm certs check-expiration.
  • Renew the API server certificate: kubeadm certs renew api-server.

Networking (CNI plugin)

  • The default path is /etc/cni/net.d/.

Kubeconfig

Manual scheduling

  • If there is no scheduler in kube-system, add nodeName to pod.yaml; otherwise, the pod remains pending.

Exam experience

5/2/2023

The exam check-in process was smoother than AWS and easy to use.

  1. The exam questions were much simpler than the difficult mock exam. The real exam had only about one-third as many questions as the mock exam.
  2. My only regret was using a laptop for convenience. It was harder to work quickly, and my vision became blurry. Next time, I will choose a large monitor.
  3. Exam topics:
    • ETCD backup and restore

    • cluster upgrade
    • cluster troubleshooting

6/2/2023

Twenty-four hours later, after receiving the result, I learned that I had failed the exam. I missed some small details during the exam, and I still had some knowledge gaps.

DaemonSet、Deployment 与 StatefulSet

  • DaemonSet 在所有节点上运行 Pod，每个节点上最多运行一个 Pod。它适合日志收集、资源监控等系统级应用，例如 Kube-proxy。

podAntiAffinity

  • 使用 requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution 时，只有满足规则，调度器才能调度 Pod。此功能类似于 nodeSelector，但语法表达能力更强。

title: The 7 Habits of Highly Effective People — Notes
content:
Starting Point

  • Fear and insecurity about life.
  • A “get it now” mentality.
  • Blaming other people.
  • Despair and helplessness—a sense of having no power.
  • A lack of direction in life.
  • The desire for a meaningful, happy, peaceful, and effective life.

1. Be Proactive: Adopt a Growth Mindset

  • Take responsibility for your past, present, and future actions, and make decisions according to principles and values rather than emotions or external circumstances.
  • Reactive people are unwilling to take responsibility for their choices. They see themselves as victims of their environment, their past, and other people.
  • Being proactive is not only an attitude toward action; it means taking responsibility for your life. Think “I can,” “I will,” and “I intend to,” rather than “if only,” “what if,” or “I cannot.”

  • The circle of concern includes everything we pay attention to in daily life, such as health, family, career, the environment, current affairs, news, entertainment, and gossip.
  • The circle of influence lies within the circle of concern and contains the things we can affect. At its core is our ability to make and keep commitments.
  • For directly controllable problems, develop the right habits. For example, to maintain the ability to earn money, keep investing in yourself and improving your productive capacity.
  • For indirectly controllable problems, work through your methods of influence.
  • For uncontrollable problems, accept reality. If the weather cannot be changed, change your response to it.
  • Focus on things you can change and control: make plans → keep learning → grow upward → expand the circle of influence → change from the inside out → become more fulfilled and creative → exert influence → change the environment.

2. Begin with the End in Mind

  • Success can still leave a person feeling empty. Ask: What kind of person do you want to be? What gives life meaning?
  • For individuals, families, and organisations, first define a vision and goals, then shape the future accordingly.

  • Security represents values, identity, and a sense of emotional belonging.
  • Guidance provides direction in life, principles for decisions, and internal standards.
  • Wisdom provides insight, judgement, and understanding.
  • Power is the ability to act and achieve goals.

3. Put First Things First

  • Order goals, vision, values, and priorities correctly. Use self-discipline to keep important things first rather than being controlled by feelings, emotions, or impulses.
  • Focus on personal and professional development first, with less focus on entertainment.
  • Organise life and take action according to importance: this is both life management and time management.
  • Identify roles → select goals → schedule progress → adjust daily.
  • Stewardship delegation focuses on final results. Give people the freedom to choose how to do the work while holding them accountable for the result.
  • Build the emotional bank account through courtesy, honesty, and trustworthiness.
  • Understand other people and sincerely accept them.
  • Keep promises and clarify expectations.
  • Act with integrity and have the courage to apologise.

4. Think Win-Win

  • Seek mutual benefit based on mutual respect rather than hostile competition.
  • Practise integrity, an abundance mentality, and empathy.
  • Maturity means being able to express your feelings and convictions while considering the thoughts and feelings of others.
  • A win-win agreement covers desired results, guidelines, available resources, accountability, and consequences or rewards.

5. Seek First to Understand, Then to Be Understood

  • Listen with both your ears and your heart, and seek genuine understanding.
  • Understand other people first, then seek to be understood.

6. Synergise

  • 1 + 1 > 2.
  • Respect differences and use creative cooperation to find a third, better solution.

7. Sharpen the Saw

  • Manage physical, spiritual, intellectual, and social-emotional resources to achieve your goals.
  • Physical renewal includes healthy eating, adequate rest, and regular exercise.
  • Spiritual and intellectual renewal includes:
    • Reading books, literary classics, and biographies to enrich cultural knowledge, broaden thinking, and improve the intellect.
    • Writing down thoughts, experiences, deep insights, and lessons learned so that thinking becomes clearer, more accurate, and more coherent.
  • Social-emotional renewal includes interpersonal leadership, empathic communication, and creative cooperation.

References

  • https://www.skillpacks.com/covey-circle-of-influence/

中文版

起点

  • 对人生的恐惧感和不安全感。
  • “现在就要得到”的心态。
  • 抱怨他人。
  • 绝望无助，感觉自己无能为力。
  • 找不到人生定位。
  • 希望拥有有意义、快乐、平和而高效的人生。

1. 积极主动：采用成长型思维

  • 为自己过去、现在和未来的行为负责，并根据原则和价值观，而不是情绪或外在环境作出决定。
  • 消极被动的人不愿为自己的选择负责，总觉得自己是受害者，受到周围环境、过去和他人的拖累。
  • 积极主动不仅是一种行事态度，还意味着要对自己的人生负责。时刻想着“我可以”“我能”“我打算”，而不是“如果”“要是”或“我不能”。

  • 关注圈包括我们日常关注的一切，例如健康、家庭、事业、环境、时事、新闻、娱乐和八卦。
  • 影响圈位于关注圈之内，包含个人能力可以影响的事情。其核心是作出承诺并信守承诺的能力。
  • 对于可以直接控制的问题，要培养正确的习惯。例如，要想一直拥有赚钱的能力，就要持续投资自己，保持并提高产能。
  • 对于可以间接控制的问题，通过改善影响方式来处理。
  • 对于无法控制的问题，要接受现实。例如，无法改变天气，就改变自己的应对方式。
  • 专注于你能够改变和控制的事情：制订计划 → 不断学习 → 向上成长 → 扩大影响圈 → 由内而外地改变 → 让自己更充实、更有创造力 → 施加影响 → 改变环境。

2. 以终为始

  • 成功之后仍可能感到空虚。要问自己：你想成为什么样的人？什么能让生活充满意义？
  • 无论个人、家庭还是组织，都应先拟定愿景和目标，再据此塑造未来。

  • 安全感代表价值观、认同和情感归属。
  • 人生方向提供决策原则和内在标准。
  • 智慧带来洞察力、判断力和理解力。
  • 力量是采取行动并达成目标的能力。

3. 要事第一

  • 正确安排目标、愿景、价值观和要事的先后顺序。 靠自制力始终把重点放在第一位，避免被感觉、情绪或冲动左右。
  • 优先关注个人和职业发展，少把注意力放在娱乐上。
  • 按照事务的重要程度安排生活并付诸行动，这既是人生管理，也是时间管理。
  • 确认角色 → 选择目标 → 安排进度 → 每日调整。
  • 责任型授权关注最终结果：让人们自由选择具体做法，同时对结果负责。
  • 通过礼貌、诚实和守信积累情感账户。
  • 理解他人，了解并真心接纳对方。
  • 信守承诺，明确期望。
  • 正直诚信，并勇于道歉。

4. 双赢思维

  • 以相互尊重为基础寻求互惠，而不是敌对竞争。
  • 坚持诚信、富足心态和换位思考。
  • 成熟意味着既能表达自己的情感和信念，也能体谅他人的想法与感受。
  • 双赢协议包括预期结果、指导方针、可用资源、责任考核，以及后果或奖励。

5. 知彼解己：先理解别人，再争取被理解

  • 用耳朵和内心倾听他人，真正理解对方。
  • 先理解别人，再争取别人的理解。

6. 统合综效

  • 1 + 1 > 2。
  • 尊重差异，通过创造性合作找到第三种、更好的解决方案。

7. 不断更新：磨利锯子

  • 管理身体、精神、智力和社会情感资源，以实现目标。
  • 身体层面的更新包括健康饮食、充足休息和定期锻炼。
  • 精神和智力层面的更新包括：
    • 阅读书籍、文学名著和名人传记，丰富文化知识，拓展思维并提高智力。
    • 写下自己的想法、经历、深刻见解和学习心得，让思路变得更清晰、准确和连贯。
  • 社会情感层面的更新包括人际领导、移情交流和创造性合作。

参考资料

  • https://www.skillpacks.com/covey-circle-of-influence/

title: Australian Shares, Tax, and Investing Basics
content:
Why Compounding and Time Matter in Investing

  • Accumulating the first $100,000 takes the longest. Keep investing regularly and let the snowball grow. Only invest money that you will not need for a long time.
  • People Tend To Overestimate What Can Be Done In One Year
  • And Underestimate What Can Be Done In Five Or Ten Years
  • Hold for the long term, trade less often, do not chase rallies or panic-sell, and invest regularly.

Basic Concepts

  1. Capital gain: the profit made when an asset is sold.
  2. Dividend: a distribution paid by a company to shareholders.
  3. Distribution: a payment made by a fund to investors.
    • After a dividend or distribution is paid, the share or unit price will generally fall by approximately the amount paid, all else being equal.
  4. Dividend reinvestment plans (DRPs) still have tax-reporting implications.
    • You cannot claim an immediate deduction for some costs related to purchasing shares, such as brokerage fees and stamp duty, but you can include them in the cost base—the ownership cost deducted from the proceeds when calculating a capital gain or loss.
    • Cash dividends are normally the default. To join a DRP, update the election through the share registry—for example, CBA uses Link Market Services and VAS uses Computershare—not through the brokerage platform.
  5. The S&P/ASX 200 is Australia’s benchmark share-market index.
  6. CHESS sponsorship:
    • Share ownership records are stored and managed electronically. A Holder Identification Number (HIN) links an investor to their holdings and transaction records. CHESS provides secure and efficient share trading, clearing, and settlement in the Australian market.
    • With a CHESS-sponsored broker, the holdings remain registered to the investor even if the trading platform fails.
    • Examples of ETF issuers and funds include BlackRock/iShares (IOZ), State Street/SPDR, BetaShares (A200), and Vanguard (VAS).

Capital Gains Tax (CGT)

  • CGT applies to a capital gain realised when an investment is sold. The net capital gain is included in assessable income and taxed at the investor’s marginal rate.
  • Australian individuals are generally eligible for a 50% CGT discount when they have owned an asset for at least 12 months, encouraging long-term investment.

Capital Losses

  • You cannot deduct a net capital loss from ordinary income, but you can carry it forward and apply it against capital gains in later years. There is no time limit for carrying forward a net capital loss.
  • This applies when shares, ETFs, or other investments are sold at a loss.
  • A capital loss can offset capital gains from other investments, but not salary or other ordinary income.
  • For example, if ETF A has a $5,000 capital gain and ETF B has a $15,000 capital loss, the net capital loss is $10,000. It can be carried forward to a later financial year but cannot be deducted from ordinary income.

Returns from Shares

  1. Capital appreciation: the difference between the purchase and sale prices.
  2. Dividends.

Bonds

  • Bonds are fixed-income investments through which governments or companies borrow money.
  • Features:
    • Relative safety.
    • Priority of repayment over shareholders.
    • Stable returns through fixed interest payments.
    • Tradability on a secondary market.
  • Australian market:
    • Government bonds: https://www.australiangovernmentbonds.gov.au/ — individual issues may have low trading volume and liquidity.
    • Corporate bonds: https://xtbs.com.au/ — individual issues may also have low trading volume and liquidity.
    • Bond ETFs combine multiple bonds, providing diversification, better liquidity, and easier trading.
      • Vanguard Australian Fixed Interest Index ETF (VAF): quarterly distributions; management fee noted as 0.2%.
      • iShares Core Composite Bond ETF (IAF): management fee noted as 0.15%.
      • BetaShares Australian Bank Senior Floating Rate Bond ETF (QPON): management fee noted as 0.22%; monthly distributions.
      • The source notes also state that financials and materials make up 40% of the ASX 200; this appears to be a separate observation rather than a characteristic of QPON.
      • Falling interest rates can reduce income from floating-rate bonds, while rising rates can make them more attractive.

Sources:

  • https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5R4aVgnhAnQ
  • https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BJv4GSLazC4

中文版

复利和时间对投资的重要性

  • 第一个 10 万澳元的积累最漫长。坚持定投，让雪球不断滚大。应该只投入长期内不需要使用的钱。
  • 人们往往高估一年内能完成的事情
  • 却低估五年或十年内能完成的事情
  • 长期持仓、降低交易频率、不追涨杀跌，并坚持定投。

一些基本概念

  1. 资本利得（Capital gain）：卖出资产时获得的利润。
  2. 股息（Dividend）：公司向股东支付的分红。
  3. 基金分配（Distribution）：基金向投资者支付的收益。
    • 在其他条件不变时，支付股息或基金分配后，股票或基金单位价格通常会下降约等于支付金额的幅度。
  4. 股息再投资计划（Dividend Reinvestment Plan，DRP）仍然涉及税务申报。
    • 购买股票时产生的某些费用（如经纪费和印花税）不能立即作为税务抵扣，但可以计入成本基础。计算资本利得或资本损失时，从处置资产所得中扣除该持有成本。
    • 默认通常是现金分红。如需加入 DRP，应通过股票登记机构修改，而不是通过股票交易平台。例如，CBA 使用 Link Market Services，VAS 使用 Computershare。
  5. S&P/ASX 200 是澳大利亚基准股票市场指数。
  6. CHESS 赞助：
    • 股票所有权记录以电子形式存储和管理。持有人识别号码（HIN）将投资者与其持仓及交易记录关联起来。CHESS 为澳大利亚市场提供安全、高效的股票交易、清算和结算。
    • 使用 CHESS 赞助的经纪商时，即使交易平台倒闭，持仓仍登记在投资者名下。
    • ETF 发行商及基金示例包括 BlackRock/iShares（IOZ）、State Street/SPDR、BetaShares（A200）和 Vanguard（VAS）。

资本利得税（CGT）

  • 投资升值并卖出后实现的资本利得需要纳税。净资本利得会计入应税收入，并按投资者的边际税率征税。
  • 澳大利亚个人持有资产至少 12 个月后再出售，通常可以享受 50% 的 CGT 折扣，这有利于长期投资。

资本损失

  • 净资本损失不能从普通收入中扣除，但可以结转，并在以后年度抵扣资本利得。净资本损失的结转没有时间限制。
  • 这适用于亏损卖出的股票、ETF 或其他投资。
  • 资本损失只能抵扣其他投资的资本利得，不能抵扣工资或其他普通收入。
  • 例如，ETF A 获得 5,000 澳元资本利得，ETF B 产生 15,000 澳元资本损失，则净资本损失为 10,000 澳元。这笔损失可以结转到后续财年，但不能从普通收入中扣除。

股票收益

  1. 资本增值：买入价与卖出价之间的差额。
  2. 股票分红。

债券

  • 债券属于固定收益类投资，政府或企业通过发行债券借款。
  • 特点：
    • 相对安全。
    • 偿还优先级高于股东。
    • 通过固定利息提供相对稳定的收益。
    • 可以在二级市场交易。
  • 澳大利亚市场：
    • 政府债券：https://www.australiangovernmentbonds.gov.au/ —— 个别债券的成交量和流动性可能较低。
    • 企业债券：https://xtbs.com.au/ —— 个别债券的成交量和流动性也可能较低。
    • 债券 ETF 由多只债券组成，可以分散风险，流动性较好，也更容易买卖。
      • Vanguard Australian Fixed Interest Index ETF（VAF）：每季度分配收益；记录的管理费为 0.2%。
      • iShares Core Composite Bond ETF（IAF）：记录的管理费为 0.15%。
      • BetaShares Australian Bank Senior Floating Rate Bond ETF（QPON）：记录的管理费为 0.22%；每月分配收益。
      • 原笔记还写到金融和材料行业占 ASX 200 的 40%；这似乎是一条独立观察，而不是 QPON 的特征。
      • 降息可能降低浮息债券的收入，而加息时这类债券可能更有吸引力。

title: The Psychology of Money
content:
• Our views about money are shaped by psychology and are subjective.
  • Your personal experience with money may represent only 0.00000001% of reality, yet it can account for 80% of how you think the world works. Two equally intelligent people can therefore hold different views about how and why recessions happen, how to invest, which issues deserve priority, and how much risk they can tolerate.
  • Luck and risk are like twins. They show that every outcome in life is influenced by forces beyond individual effort.
  • Modern capitalism is good at producing two things: wealth and envy. Wealth motivates people to work hard, but without contentment there is no happiness in life.
  • Many things in the world are not worth risking, no matter how large the potential reward.

Wealth, Compounding, and Survival

  • Compounding plus time is the key to Warren Buffett’s success.
  • Becoming wealthy requires risk-taking, optimism, and the courage to make a bold move.
  • Staying wealthy requires frugality and an acknowledgement that some of your wealth came from luck. Do not assume that past success can be repeated indefinitely.
  • You need short-term vigilance to survive long enough to enjoy optimistic long-term outcomes.
  • Anything enormous, profitable, famous, or influential results from a tail event—one event that stands out among thousands or even millions. When we focus only on its outcome, it is easy to underestimate how rare and powerful the tail event itself was.
  • The principle that “a small number of things drive most results” applies not only to companies in a portfolio, but also to an investor’s own behaviour.
  • Your success as an investor is determined by how you respond to occasional moments of terror, not by how you spend the many uneventful years. An investing genius should remain rational when everyone nearby becomes irrational.

Freedom, Restraint, and Sustainable Goals

  • The greatest reward of wealth is the ability to do what you want, when and where you want, with whomever you want, for as long as you want.
  • Restraint is a prerequisite for becoming wealthy.
  • People change. They readily recognise how much they have changed since the past but tend to underestimate how much their personality, ideas, and goals will change in the future. Psychologists call this the “End of History Illusion.”
  • The first rule of compounding is never to interrupt it unnecessarily.
  • At every stage of a career, set balanced goals: maintain moderate annual savings, allow yourself a reasonable amount of free time, keep commuting within reasonable limits, and spend sufficient time with family. Avoiding extremes makes a plan easier to sustain and reduces the chance of future regret.

The Seduction of Pessimism

  • For reasons I cannot understand, people always seem eager to hear that the world is coming to an end.
  • The greatest dividend wealth can provide is the ability to do what you enjoy, with people you like, whenever you want and for as long as you want.

Notes from 堆金积玉

Source: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tipw9c57eQU

  1. Different people understand money differently, and everyone’s perspective is limited.
  2. Saving is necessary to avoid falling into consumerism.
  3. Frugality helps preserve wealth.
  4. Leave room for investment mistakes and build in a margin of safety—a backup plan.
  5. Your behaviour matters more than your financial skills.
  6. Contentment brings happiness.
  7. Freedom has the highest value; work toward “f-you money.”
  8. Wait patiently for good results.
  9. Live within your means.
  10. Do not let other people unduly influence you.

中文版

  • 我们对金钱的观念受心理支配，具有主观性。
  • 你对金钱的个人经验可能只占现实的 0.00000001%，却构成了你对世界运行方式判断的 80%。因此，两个同样聪明的人可能会对经济衰退发生的机制和原因、如何投资、哪些问题应优先处理，以及自己能承受多大风险持有不同看法。
  • 运气和风险就像孪生兄弟。它们证明，生活中的每一个结果都会受到个人努力之外的力量影响。
  • 现代资本主义擅长创造两样东西：财富和嫉妒。财富是人们拼命工作的动力，但如果不懂知足，生活就没有快乐。
  • 世界上有许多东西不值得冒险，无论潜在收益有多大。

财富、复利与生存

  • 复利加时间才是巴菲特成功的关键。
  • 致富需要冒险精神、乐观心态，以及放手一搏的勇气。
  • 守富需要节俭，也要承认财富中有一部分源于运气。不要指望过去的成功可以无限复制。
  • 你需要保持短期警觉，先让自己生存下来，才能看到长期的乐观结果。
  • 任何规模巨大、利润丰厚、声名远播或影响深远的事物，都源于某个尾部事件——从成千上万甚至数百万个事件中脱颖而出的一个。当我们只关注尾部事件的结果时，很容易低估事件本身的稀缺性和强大影响。
  • “少数几件事决定主要结果”这一规律，不仅适用于投资组合中的公司，也适用于投资者自身的行为。
  • 作为投资者，成功取决于你如何应对偶尔出现的恐惧瞬间，而不是如何度过年复一年的平淡时期。投资天才也应该能在身边所有人都失去理性时继续理性行事。

自由、克制与可持续的目标

  • 财富最令人惊叹的回报，是让你能够在任何时间、任何地点，与任何人一起，做任何想做的事，而且想做多久就做多久。
  • 克制是富有的前提。
  • 人是会变的。人们能敏锐地意识到自己相比过去发生了多少变化，却容易低估自己的性格、想法和目标未来还会发生多少变化。心理学家把这一现象称为“历史终结错觉”（The End of History Illusion）。
  • 复利的第一条原则是：除非万不得已，永远不要打断这个过程。
  • 无论处于职业生涯的哪个阶段，都要设定均衡的目标：每年适度储蓄，给自己适量的自由时间，把通勤控制在合理范围内，并花足够的时间陪伴家人。避免任何一方面走向极端，会让计划更容易坚持，并降低未来后悔的可能。

悲观主义的诱惑

  • 出于一些我无法理解的原因，人们似乎总喜欢听别人说世界要完蛋了。
  • 财富能带来的最大红利，是让你可以随时和喜欢的人一起做喜欢的事，而且想做多久就做多久。

出自“堆金积玉”的笔记

来源：https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tipw9c57eQU

  1. 不同的人对金钱有不同认知，而且每个人的视角都有局限。
  2. 需要储蓄，以免陷入消费主义。
  3. 通过节俭来守住财富。
  4. 给错误的投资留有余地，设置安全边际，并准备备用方案。
  5. 你的行为比理财技能更重要。
  6. 知足常乐。
  7. 自由的价值最高；努力积累“f-you money”。
  8. 耐心静候佳音。
  9. 量入为出。
  10. 不要让他人过度影响自己。

title: From Broke to Multi-Millionaire in Just 7 Years — Notes
content:
My Thoughts

The book is interesting and covers a great deal of basic knowledge about building wealth. However, accumulating the initial capital for investing often feels like the hardest part. If the sequence of events in the book is accurate, I admire the author: succeeding required him to think strategically.

Useful Excerpts and Lessons

  • Applying knowledge to your life is the secret to becoming wealthy. Use what you already have to build wealth; if you lack something, learn it.
  • You get what you focus on. If you focus too heavily on difficulties, you can no longer see any opportunities. If you want to become wealthy, do not look only at obstacles.
  • Becoming wealthy does not depend on whether you are kind, good, or hardworking; it depends on how many other people are capable of doing your job. Build irreplaceable skills.
  • Any method that lets you influence or sell to more than one person at the same time is a form of leverage. This is the basis of passive income.
  • Wealthy people always save part of their money for investment first, then spend what remains. Take a long-term view of money and benefit from compounding.

References

  • Author: https://www.peterspann.com.au/
  • Book: From Broke to Multi-Millionaire in Just 7 Years by Peter Spann

中文版

我的感想

这本书很有意思，涵盖了许多积累财富的基本知识。不过，投资的第一桶金往往最难积累。如果书中叙述的事件顺序准确，我很佩服作者：要想取胜，必须有策略地思考。

对我有用的摘录与启发

  • 把知识应用于生活，就是致富的秘诀。 用自己已经拥有的东西创造财富；如果有所欠缺，就去学习。
  • 你关注什么，就会得到什么。因此，当你过度关注困难时，就再也看不到任何机会。 想要富有，就不要只盯着困难。
  • 能否致富并不取决于你是否善良、是否是好人，或是否努力，而取决于有多少人能够胜任你的工作。 要培养不可替代的能力。
  • 任何能够让你同时影响一个以上的人，或向一个以上的人销售的方法，都是杠杆作用的体现。 这是被动收入的基础。
  • 富有的人总是先存下一部分钱用于投资，然后才消费剩余的钱。 要用长远的眼光看待金钱，发挥复利的作用。

参考资料

  • 作者：https://www.peterspann.com.au/
  • 书名：Peter Spann 的 From Broke to Multi-Millionaire in Just 7 Years

title: The Rational Optimist

Life Today Is Better Than Ever

  • Humanity’s continuing progress is built on exchange, the specialisation and division of labour, and continual innovation.

今天的生活比以往任何时候都好

  • 与前人相比，我们今天的生活幸福、舒适得多。我们拥有空调、舒适的床和多种多样的食物，因此没有必要一味悲观。
